record.original_question: Let N={1,2,3,...}. For A⊆N and α≥−1, define the α-weighted upper and lower densities by the weighted-density construction with weight f(n)=n^α; α=0 gives asymptotic density and α=−1 gives logarithmic density. For a fixed set A, the upper α-density as a function of α is increasing and the lower α-density as a function of α is decreasing, with the necessary condition that such functions are continuous except possibly at α=−1. Which increasing functions f:[−1,∞)→[0,1] can occur as the upper α-density function α↦upper_d_α(A) of some A⊆N, and which decreasing functions f:[−1,∞)→[0,1] can occur as the lower α-density function α↦lower_d_α(A) of some A⊆N?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$. For a real parameter $\alpha\ge -1$, define the $\alpha$-weighted upper and lower densities of a set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ by
$$\overline{d}_\alpha(A)=\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\sum_{n\le N,\ n\in A}n^{\alpha}}{\sum_{n\le N}n^{\alpha}},\qquad \underline{d}_\alpha(A)=\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\sum_{n\le N,\ n\in A}n^{\alpha}}{\sum_{n\le N}n^{\alpha}}.$$
The case $\alpha=0$ recovers the asymptotic (natural) density and the case $\alpha=-1$ recovers the logarithmic density. For a fixed $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, the map $\alpha\mapsto\overline{d}_\alpha(A)$ is non-decreasing, the map $\alpha\mapsto\underline{d}_\alpha(A)$ is non-increasing, and both maps are continuous on $[-1,+\infty)$ except possibly at $\alpha=-1$.

Characterize the class of functions occurring as such profiles. Specifically:

(a) Determine precisely which non-decreasing functions $f:[-1,+\infty)\to[0,1]$ arise as $\alpha\mapsto\overline{d}_\alpha(A)$ for some $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$.

(b) Determine precisely which non-increasing functions $g:[-1,+\infty)\to[0,1]$ arise as $\alpha\mapsto\underline{d}_\alpha(A)$ for some $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up the general framework of weighted/α-densities and works characterizing axiomatic upper densities, but no result that identifies precisely which monotone functions on [−1,∞) arise as the α-density profile α↦d̄_α(A) or α↦d_α(A) of a subset of ℕ. The problem appears to remain open; only the qualitative properties (monotonicity, continuity except possibly at α=−1) are established.

status_evidence.title: On the notions of upper and lower density
status_evidence.snippet: Axiomatic study of upper densities; α-densities discussed as examples but no characterization of profile functions.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work characterizes axiomatic upper densities, not the α-density profile of fixed sets.

status_evidence.title: Density sets of sets of positive integers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sets of densities attainable by subsets of ℕ under various density notions.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterization questions are studied, but the specific profile problem on [-1,∞) is not resolved.
